label: Tabletop
description: Handmade objects on one tabletop, seen from above. They're set down, arranged, moved and labelled in handwriting, with arrows and circles, like a teacher explaining with things on a table. Stop-motion timing, real shadows.
suits: science, how things work, money, health, anything with parts, amounts, causes and steps
cost: a few cents a video: each object is drawn once and reused
surface: An empty tabletop seen from directly above, filling the whole frame edge to edge: {surface}. Soft, even daylight from the top left with a gentle falloff toward the bottom right. Nothing on it at all: no objects, no text. Photographic, like the set of a stop-motion animation.
kit_view: Photographed from directly above, lying flat on a table, whole object visible with a margin all round, soft even daylight from the top left, no cast shadow, isolated on a transparent background.
guide: Everything happens on one tabletop, seen from directly above. Real, handmade objects stand for the ideas: a brain for the brain, a coin for money, a little house for a home, a heart for love. They're set down as they're mentioned, arranged, moved and labelled; handwritten labels, arrows and circles make the explanation clear. Think like a teacher explaining with things on a table, and make it playful and tactile. An object a later beat still needs stays on the table and moves to its new place (keep the same key), so the table is one continuous performance. Choose objects a craftsperson could make as a small, simple object; never a scene, a landscape or a crowd of people. People are simple doll-like figures, used sparingly.
